objective: Define the smallest build-only validation boundary for the accepted repo-owned Verilator overlay patch before any native parser support, execution, timing, or automatic allocation claim.

definition_decision.weakest_point: A successful build would prove only that the patched Verilator source compiles and links far enough to produce verilator_bin. It would still not prove parser behavior, sidecar handoff, runtime execution, timing, upstream acceptance, or arbitrary RTL/filelist support.
reason: the descriptor/apply-check implementation has already been reviewed and accepted narrowly
the next unknown is compile/link compatibility of the patch against pinned Verilator v5.048
Verilator v5.048 Makefile.in exposes a verilator_bin target, which is narrower than upstream regression tests and broader than a source-only apply check
parser behavior and option validation should remain separate from build-only validation unless a later gate explicitly selects them

build_only_validation_boundary.selected_build_target_rationale: Verilator v5.048 Makefile.in defines a phony verilator_bin target that builds the main optimized binary without running upstream test_regress.
build_only_validation_boundary.log_capture_policy: If the next execution gate captures logs, store them under reports/ as generated evidence only and do not write local absolute paths into source-of-truth files.
build_only_validation_boundary.artifacts_policy: The external checkout and build outputs are local/generated state, not repo source of truth.

parser_behavior_execution: accept --sim-accel sidecar-gpu --sim-accel-states N --sim-accel-steps S through the built binary

required_next_gate.name: review_verilator_native_option_parser_overlay_patch_build_only_validation_gate
must_decide: whether the selected command sequence is narrow enough to remain build-only
whether verilator_bin is the right first build target before parser-behavior execution
whether the command sequence avoids vendoring Verilator or writing under third_party
whether the deferred parser-behavior and std::atoi caveats are explicit enough
whether the following gate should run the build-only validation or revise the boundary
must_not_claim: Verilator upstream regression tests pass with this patch

non_claims: not a landed upstream Verilator patch
not a runtime or ABI change
not GEM benchmark or comparison evidence
reports and artifacts are generated evidence, not source of truth
